links.outcome: AI vs registered dietitian accuracy for energy and macronutrient estimation against weighed ground truth
links.effect: For energy and carbohydrates, RDs and top AI models had r > 0.8, often within ±10%. Protein and lipid accuracy was significantly lower across all AI models, with lipid overestimation Mean Bias > +20%.
links.quote: For energy and carbohydrates, RDs and top-performing AI models (notably ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro) demonstrated practical accuracy (r > 0.8, frequently within ±10% range).

unlisted_practices: Integrating cooking metadata with meal images to improve AI nutrient estimation

screen.reason: Empirical reader/accuracy study comparing 10 multimodal AI models (including GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro) with registered dietitians for estimating nutrients from hospital meal images; evaluates model performance against human benchmark without testing a specific deployment safeguard/practice.
